title: Exact partial-cycle search factors for de Bruijn sequences
summary: Determine every unknown intermediate search factor $q_d$ in the partial-cycle algorithm for finding de Bruijn characteristic functions.

formal_statement.body: For the source-defined acyclic partial-cycle families $\mathcal F(d)$, let $$q_d=\frac{|\mathcal F(d-1)|2^{\binom{n-1}{d}}}{|\mathcal F(d)|}.$$ Determine $q_d$ exactly for every admissible order $n$ and every $2\le d\le n-2$. The endpoint values $q_0=2$, $q_1=2^{n-1}/(2^{n-1}-2)$, and $q_{n-1}=2$ do not settle the intermediate values.

scope.domain: Partial-cycle extensions in a search algorithm for de Bruijn characteristic functions
assumptions: $\mathcal F(d)$ is the source's family of degree-at-most-$d$ characteristic functions whose partial cycle structure is acyclic
$\alpha_d$ is chosen uniformly from binary degree-$d$ coefficient vectors
$q_d$ is the average repeat-until count at degree $d$
scope.unresolved_remainder: Exact formulas remain unknown for all source-unspecified intermediate values $q_d$, namely $2\le d\le n-2$ over the full admissible order range.

citations.label: Li--Lin, partial-cycle Algorithm 2 search factors
citations.locator: Section VI, Algorithm 2 analysis, journal p. 606

progress.summary: The source derives three endpoint factors and explicitly states that all other $q_d$ values are unknown.
